name: farm
summary: Work packets: hand gated, self-contained tasks to an external AI service -- or to an engine on your own hardware, cheapest rung first, climbing only when a check fails -- and ingest the answers as unverified

settings.summary: Ladder mode for farmed packets: try a local engine first, climb to a bigger one, then a hosted one (public material only), then Claude, only when a check fails.
settings.detail:
off  `gt_farm_send.py ladder` refuses to run (send, relay and ledger are unaffected)  (default)
on   `ladder PACKET --class C` starts at the task class's rung from farm-ladder.tsv, runs the
     class's check on the reply, escalates on failure and stops with "escalate to Claude"
     (exit 5) at the top; every attempt is a savings-ledger line

The table of task classes ships in the module (templates/farm-ladder.tsv, also built into
gt_farm_ladder.py) and is overridden per vault by <vault>/farm-ladder.tsv. Hosted rung 3 is
reached only for a class marked public (or --public) and a packet that clears the Releasable
gate after the scrub. GT_FARM_LADDER=off|on in the environment overrides this setting.

settings.summary: Share of accepted ladder results marked for a blind Claude audit (a class's own audit_rate in farm-ladder.tsv wins).
settings.detail:
0    never sample: the audit loop is off and a class's start rung never moves
0.2  one accepted result in five is marked `audit: pending` in the savings ledger  (default)
1    every accepted result is marked

A Claude subagent grades a marked result blind; `gt_farm_send.py audit-result KEY pass|fail`
records it. Two failed audits in a class raise its start rung by one, five clean audits in a
row lower it by one. GT_FARM_AUDIT_RATE in the environment overrides this setting.

settings.summary: Run gt ingest stages (extract, classify, draft) on a big local engine with the v4 packaging instead of in Claude.
settings.detail:
off  every stage runs in Claude  (default)
on   `gt_farm_send.py pipeline` may run a stage whose class starts at rung 2 or lower on a
     `local: yes` engine: the unit's material inline and unsplit, one exemplar, the output
     fields spelled out, the schema bound, one self-audit, validate and retry once; an answer
     still not valid is reported (exit 3) and the stage runs in Claude

An engine that is not local is refused: stage material is vault content. Needs a service-table
row with `local: yes` (rung 2). GT_PIPELINE_ENGINE=off|on in the environment overrides this setting.

settings.summary: Break-even size for an automatic send: a packet smaller than this many characters is not worth the Claude tokens the send itself costs, so it stays in Claude.
settings.detail:
0     never skip: every automatic send goes
2000  an automatic send (ladder, pipeline, `send --auto` as gt-intake and workflow farm steps use it)
      of a smaller packet is skipped with "not worth sending: N chars < break-even M" (exit 5)  (default)

A `send --service X` typed by the user is never skipped. The default comes from the farm ledger on
the owner's machine: Claude's fixed cost of a send (~220 tokens) plus the packet scaffold the engine
reads (~120) is ~340 tokens, ~1,360 characters, with a 1.5x margin. GT_FARM_MIN_CHARS=N in the
environment, or --min-chars N for one run, overrides this setting.

settings.summary: How long a passing farmed result is reused instead of sending the same packet to the same engine and model again.
settings.detail:
0   never reuse: every send goes to the engine
7   a passing result under 7 days old is filed again without a send, reported as "reused" and
    marked `reused: true` in the savings ledger  (default)

The key is sha256(packet + engine + model). `--fresh` forces a new send. Stored results live in
~/.claude/golden-thread/farm/cache (folder 0700, files 0600). GT_FARM_REUSE_DAYS=N overrides.

settings.summary: How often a long send says it is still waiting, in seconds. 0 turns the waiting line off.
settings.detail:
0    no waiting line (the start and finish line of each packet are still printed)
30   every 30 seconds a "waiting" line names each engine still working, for how long, and how many
     packets are left  (default)

The lines go to stderr; `--json` output on stdout is unchanged. A send can run up to 15 minutes
(`send`, `ladder`) or an hour (`pipeline`). GT_FARM_HEARTBEAT_S=N in the environment overrides this setting.
